findings.title: TradeRecord.from_row restates the trade column order positionally
findings.description: The candle path is mapping-driven and loud: `CandleRecord.from_row` walks `CANDLE_COLUMNS` with `zip(..., strict=True)`, and `test_nested_field_set_is_exactly_what_candle_columns_describes` fails on any name change. The trade path is not. `TradeRecord.from_row` indexes `values[0]`…`values[7]` by hand, so the coupling to `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS` (which `fetch_trades` derives from `TRADE_COLUMNS`) is implicit only. Consequences if `TRADE_COLUMNS` ever gains a column: a column appended mid-order shifts every subsequent field silently (`taker_outcome_side` receives the new column's value, wrong data served with 200s); a column appended at the end is silently dropped. The existing guards do not catch this: the integration test `test_value_count_matches_the_repository_mapping` compares `len(r.values)` to `len(TRADE_COLUMNS) - 1` — both sides derive from the same constant, so it passes regardless — and the unit tests construct `TradeRow` with exactly 8 hand-written values. The module docstring's design claim ("a column added there is served here without an edit") is true for candles and false for trades. Relatedly, `TradeRow.values` is typed `tuple[Any, ...]` while its sibling `CandleRow.values` is `tuple[Decimal | None, ...]` — the looseness is what makes the positional restatement type-invisible. Driving `from_row` from `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS` with a strict zip (mirroring `CandleRecord`) would make the two halves of the same module consistent and the failure loud.

findings.title: Ceiling-sized responses are built and serialized on the event loop
findings.description: After the executor call returns, `CandlesResponse.build(...)` (75,000 `CandleRecord.from_row` pydantic constructions) and `timeseries_response(...)` (a `model_dump` plus an orjson dump of the recorded 34.80 MB payload) run directly on the event-loop thread; `get_trades` has the same shape. The project's async rule is explicit that synchronous code inside an `async def` must be <1 ms worst case or move to an executor — building and serializing a ceiling-sized response is CPU-bound work measured in the hundreds of milliseconds (the load tier's own 1.034 s end-to-end figure bounds it). During one such request, every other request on the process — including `/health`, which the 185 D8a connection-scoping work specifically exists to protect — stalls. I note this follows the established `bars.py` pattern (`BarsResponse.from_dataframe` + serialization also run on the loop), so it is an accepted trade-off rather than a new invention; but this slice makes it materially worse (34.80 MB vs the 11.58 MB bars figure, sixteen decimal strings per row), and the concurrency load test (`test_concurrent_market_detail_requests`) exercises only fast market seeks, so the loop-blocking dimension of a ceiling-sized response is unmeasured by the new tier. The fix is cheap and compatible with the D8a scoping: build and serialize inside the same executor call (they need neither the loop nor a connection).

findings.title: tape_complete_through description contradicts the value it carries
findings.description: The field description reads "Created time of the newest stored trade", but the value is the trades surface's `sync_state.watermark_ts` (see `tape_facts` in `src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/serve_timeseries.py`, which returns `tape_complete_through=watermark`). Those are different things, and the slice's own integration test proves it: `TestTapeFacts.test_returns_the_effective_floor_and_watermark` seeds a watermark with *zero* trades stored and asserts a non-null `tape_complete_through`. The watermark is the completeness edge the phase advanced to — on a quiet market it sits ahead of the newest stored trade, exactly the distinction the candles field's description spells out ("not 'the newest stored candle'"). The field *name* is right; the description served through OpenAPI will mislead clients about quiet periods.

findings.title: "Fourteen value columns" miscounts — the mapping has sixteen
findings.description: `CandleRow`'s docstring says "its period end plus the fourteen value columns", but `CANDLE_COLUMNS` has sixteen entries: 4 (`yes_bid`) + 4 (`yes_ask`) + 6 (`price`, OHLC + previous + mean) re-nested, plus `volume_fp` and `open_interest_fp` flat — and `values` is populated from all of them. The `models/kalshi_timeseries.py` module docstring's "the fourteen flat stored columns are re-nested" is similarly ambiguous (fourteen is the re-nested subset, not the flat total). The slice's own load tier and `constants.py` both correctly say "sixteen decimal strings", so the codebase now carries both counts. No behavioral impact — no test or code reads "fourteen" — but the wrong count is in the exact docstrings a future editor will trust when touching the mapping.

findings.title: Hardcoded 450 duplicates KALSHI_MARKET_COUNT
findings.description: `test_markets_list_scoped_to_the_dense_event` asserts `body["count"] == 450`, restating the `KALSHI_MARKET_COUNT = 450` constant defined in `test/load/conftest.py` — a value the test module already imports four of its sibling constants from. The project convention is one definition referenced everywhere; raising the fixture's market count would break this test with a misleading failure (a fixture-shape drift message pointing at the API, not at the duplicated literal). Compare `test_events_list_at_production_width`, where `24_382` is a deliberately inline measured production fact with a justifying docstring — the 450 has no such reason to exist as a literal.
